europe.overview: Europe occupies the western part of Eurasia and has an extensively indented coastline.
europe.location: Northern Hemisphere, extending across the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
europe.boundaries: The conventional boundary with Asia follows the Urals, Ural River, Caspian Sea, Caucasus and Black Sea straits. Continental boundaries are conventions, not national borders.
europe.oceans: Atlantic Ocean and Arctic Ocean; major adjacent seas include the Mediterranean, Baltic and Black Seas.
europe.terrain: Major landscapes include the European Plain, Scandinavian uplands, Alps, Carpathians and extensive peninsulas.
europe.climate: Conditions range from Arctic and subarctic climates to temperate maritime, continental and Mediterranean climates.
europe.classification: Europe and Asia are separate geographic groupings here, despite sharing the Eurasian landmass. Transcontinental countries can belong to both.
europe.registry_note: The count includes registered countries and territories, not only sovereign states. It is calculated from current registry memberships.

africa.overview: Africa is the second-largest continent and extends across the Equator.
africa.location: Northern and Southern Hemispheres; the prime meridian also crosses the continent.
africa.boundaries: The Mediterranean separates Africa from Europe. The Red Sea and the Suez region mark its northeastern connection with Asia.
africa.oceans: Atlantic Ocean to the west and Indian Ocean to the east; the Mediterranean and Red Seas form important northern boundaries.
africa.terrain: Major landscapes include the Sahara, Sahel, Congo Basin, East African Rift, Ethiopian Highlands and southern plateaus.
africa.climate: Climate zones include equatorial rainforest, tropical savanna, hot desert, highland and Mediterranean environments.
africa.classification: Africa is a geographic continent, not an administrative parent or a political union. Egypt has African and Asian geographic memberships in this registry.
africa.registry_note: Country and territory memberships are counted together. Regional organizations and their membership totals are separate concepts.

asia.overview: Asia is the largest continent and forms the eastern part of the Eurasian landmass.
asia.location: Predominantly in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres, with islands extending south of the Equator.
asia.boundaries: Its western boundary with Europe is conventional. The Suez region connects it with Africa, and the Bering Strait separates it from North America.
asia.oceans: Arctic Ocean to the north, Pacific Ocean to the east and Indian Ocean to the south.
asia.terrain: The Himalayas, Tibetan Plateau, Siberian plains, major river basins, deserts and island arcs illustrate its geographic diversity.
asia.climate: Climates range from polar and subarctic to continental, arid, monsoon and humid tropical conditions.
asia.classification: A country may have multiple continental memberships. Geographic membership is independent of political or sporting affiliations.
asia.registry_note: The count reflects registered countries and territories assigned to Asia, including transcontinental entries.

north-america.overview: North America extends from the Arctic to the Central American isthmus and includes the Caribbean geographic region.
north-america.location: Predominantly in the Northern and Western Hemispheres.
north-america.boundaries: The Bering Strait separates it from Asia. Central America connects it to South America at the Isthmus of Panama.
north-america.oceans: Arctic Ocean to the north, Atlantic Ocean to the east and Pacific Ocean to the west.
north-america.terrain: The western cordilleras, Canadian Shield, interior plains, Appalachian Mountains and coastal lowlands form major physical regions.
north-america.climate: Conditions range from Arctic and subarctic through temperate and arid zones to tropical Central American and Caribbean climates.
north-america.classification: This grouping includes Central America, the Caribbean and Greenland. It is broader than the statistical subregion called Northern America.
north-america.registry_note: Territories are classified geographically, not automatically under the continent of their administering state.

south-america.overview: South America extends from the Caribbean region toward the southern end of the Americas.
south-america.location: Western Hemisphere, mostly south of the Equator, with northern areas in the Northern Hemisphere.
south-america.boundaries: The Isthmus of Panama joins it to North America. The Drake Passage lies between its southern end and the Antarctic Peninsula.
south-america.oceans: Pacific Ocean to the west and Atlantic Ocean to the east.
south-america.terrain: Principal landscapes include the Andes, Amazon Basin, Guiana and Brazilian highlands, Pampas and Patagonia.
south-america.climate: Equatorial rainforest, tropical savanna, arid coastal, temperate, mountain and subpolar environments occur across the continent.
south-america.classification: South America is separate from North America in this registry's seven-group model. Latin America is a cultural grouping and is not synonymous with this continent.
south-america.registry_note: The count includes countries and territories geographically assigned to South America, regardless of their administrative affiliation.

oceania.overview: Oceania is a broad geographic grouping comprising Australia and Pacific island regions.
oceania.location: Pacific-centred region spanning both sides of the Equator and the international date line.
oceania.boundaries: Its limits depend on the classification used; geographic, geological, statistical and sporting definitions do not always agree.
oceania.oceans: Pacific Ocean and the Indian Ocean around western Australia.
oceania.terrain: Continental land, mountainous and volcanic islands, coral atolls, reefs and extensive marine environments characterize the region.
oceania.climate: Environments range from arid Australian interiors to tropical islands, temperate New Zealand and alpine landscapes.
oceania.classification: Oceania is used here as a regional registry group. It is not identical to the geological continent of Australia. Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia are associated regional groupings.
oceania.registry_note: Country assignments follow the registry's geographic catalogue and can differ from sporting confederations. Ocean surface is not land area.

antarctica.overview: Antarctica is the ice-covered continent surrounding the South Pole.
antarctica.location: Southern Hemisphere, largely south of the Antarctic Circle, spanning all longitudes.
antarctica.boundaries: The continental coastline, Antarctic region and Antarctic Treaty area are different geographic or legal concepts. The Treaty applies south of 60 degrees south latitude.
antarctica.terrain: A vast ice sheet covers most of the land, with mountain ranges, exposed rock, ice shelves and the Antarctic Peninsula.
antarctica.climate: Polar desert conditions predominate, with extreme cold, strong winds and seasonal daylight differences.
antarctica.classification: Antarctica has no sovereign countries. Territorial claims do not constitute ordinary national subdivisions, and this registry does not adjudicate sovereignty.
antarctica.registry_note: The count includes Antarctica and southern territories assigned to this catalogue group. It is not a count of sovereign countries or a statement that every entry lies on the continental mainland.
